content.title: About
content.content: The dried vegetable mixture is made from finely ground dried vegetables such as carrot, onion, pepper, celery and others. The vegetables are blanched, sliced and dried at low temperature, preserving most of their nutrients and aromas. The blend is convenient, does not require refrigeration and is ideal for quick meal preparation.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dried vegetable mixes are popular in backpacking meals and vegetarian cooking.
A single blend can contain up to ten different vegetables, providing a broad spectrum of vitamins and minerals.
Low‑temperature drying retains up to 80 % of the original vitamin C content.
The mixture easily dissolves in hot water, creating a flavorful broth.
Manufacturers often add herbs such as parsley or basil to enhance taste.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vegetables provide B1, B2, B3 and B6 vitamins that support energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Drying preserves most of the plant fiber, which aids normal digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The blend contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Carotenoids and polyphenols that survive the drying process help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Vitamin C and other micronutrients contribute to a healthy immune system.

items.title: Allergy to specific vegetables
items.content: People allergic to certain vegetables (e.g., onion) may react to the blend.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some mixes are fortified with salt; those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Loss of heat‑sensitive vitamins
items.content: Heat during drying can reduce levels of vitamins such as vitamin C.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add the dried vegetable mixture to soups, sauces, stews, porridge, or simply pour hot water over it to make a flavorful broth. It can serve as a base for vegetarian patties or casseroles. For extra depth, briefly toast the mixture in a dry pan before using.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage (over 6 months) keep it in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation and flavor loss.
